CVE-2026-101340.title: Query ID predictable from a short sequence of observations
CVE-2026-101340.description: Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests. In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function. An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted. The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker. Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

CVE-2026-14440.title: Cloudflare Universal SSL automatically managed CAA RRset supersedes customer-configured CAA records
CVE-2026-14440.description:
Description:

To issue and renew TLS certificates on behalf of customers, Cloudflare's Universal SSL feature automatically manages the CAA RRset for the customer's zone. This auto-managed RRset is permissive by design (e.g. 'issue "letsencrypt.org"' without parameters). On Universal SSL zones, Cloudflare's authoritative DNS serves this auto-managed RRset at query time, superseding any customer-configured CAA records on the zone. When a customer publishes a stricter CAA record using the RFC 8657 accounturi or validationmethods parameters, the Certificate Authority does not observe those parameters when evaluating the served RRset under RFC 8659. As a result, the RFC 8657 account-binding and validation-method-binding protections are not enforced end-to-end on Universal SSL zones. Successful exploitation could result in issuance of a browser-trusted TLS certificate to an attacker, enabling MITM against the affected domain.

CVE-2026-98884.title: mmc: core: Add validation for host-provided max_segs
CVE-2026-98884.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mmc: core: Add validation for host-provided max_segs

The max_segs field is of type unsigned short, and if a host driver
sets an excessively large value, it may be truncated to zero. This
can cause mmc_alloc_sg() to call kmalloc_objs() with a zero size
allocation request, which leads to undefined behavior.

Under the SLUB allocator, kmalloc(0) returns a special pointer

CVE-2026-98963.title: btrfs: always return -EIOCBQUEUED after btrfs_uring_read_extent_endio
CVE-2026-98963.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: always return -EIOCBQUEUED after btrfs_uring_read_extent_endio

If all bios finish before btrfs_encoded_read_regular_fill_pages()
returns, it calls btrfs_uring_read_extent_endio() and previously
returned the I/O status. A negative errno then made
btrfs_uring_read_extent() unlock and free while
btrfs_uring_read_finished() did the same again.

Return -EIOCBQUEUED so only the deferred path cleans up.

CVE-2026-99379.title: smb: client: validate SMB1 EA list bounds before parsing
CVE-2026-99379.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: validate SMB1 EA list bounds before parsing

CIFSSMBQAllEAs() checks the server-provided EA list length by adding it
to the response pointer. On 32-bit systems, a positive length can wrap
the pointer and pass the comparison. The parser then walks outside the
received response while reading the next FEA header.

A response with a list length of 0x40000000 reproduces this as a native
i386 page fault and kernel panic from listxattr() against an SMB1
server.

Check that the EA list starts within the SMB byte area before reading
its header. Keep its length unsigned and compare it with the bytes left
in the response without pointer addition.

SMB1 is not negotiated by default and requires an explicit vers=1.0
mount.
